## Deliverable
The `docs` source of GW-CATALOG-GO refreshes `ok` again: each model's monthly limit per plan and the peak-price facts are read from wherever the vendor now publishes them, since the Go page (`go.mdx`) no longer carries them.

**Not queueable yet — one operator fact is missing (see §The fork).** Everything else below is verified and ready to become the queue body once the fork is taken.

## What broke (verified live 2026-11-18T05:10Z)
- `GoCatalogParseFailed{source="docs"}` active since 2026-11-16T23:37:29Z; `GoCatalogStale{source="docs"}` active since 2026-11-17T18:02:29Z. `gateway_go_catalog_age_seconds{source="docs"}` = 127772; `gateway_go_catalog_models{source="docs"}` = 34 (the last good, fetched 2026-11-16T17:31:32Z, is in use); `gateway_go_catalog_refresh_total{source="docs",outcome="parse-failed"}` = 3, `ok` = 0 on this pod.
- The gateway's log at every refresh (2026-11-17 15:45, 21:45, 2026-11-18 03:45): `catalog: docs parse failed (docs read — ParseError: no Endpoints table (Model | Model ID)) — keeping the last good snapshot`.
- The vendor page today (`raw.githubusercontent.com/anomalyco/opencode/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/console/go.mdx`, HTTP 200, 263 lines) has **no** Endpoints table, **no** per-plan limit/price tabs, **no** `(Peak)` rows and **no** peak-hours sentence. Its tables are the Plan table (`**Go**` $10, `**Go Plus**` $40, `**Go Teams**`), two client tables and a Privacy retention table. Vendor commit `222a5abef` (2026-11-17T00:30Z, "docs(go): link Go's per-model lists and tables to Console's Go page (#64271)") moved them to `https://opencode.ai/console/go#limits` / `#pricing` / `#api`.
- The share sentence changed shape too, one commit earlier (`d481307bb`, 2026-11-16T19:23Z, "explain how models share the usage allowance"): the fixture's `Each model has the following usage limits: 5-hour — 20% of the monthly limit; …` is now three bullets (`- The **5-hour limit** is 20% of your monthly allowance. …`, `- The **weekly limit** is 50% of your monthly allowance. …`). The alert's onset (23:37Z on 11-16) is before #64271 landed, so this is probably what failed the first refresh — the pod's log does not reach back that far.
- Nothing admission reads is wrong today: the frozen snapshot's limits still match the vendor's (e.g. `deepseek-v4.1-flash` $100 in the view and in the vendor's answer below). It will not self-heal — every refresh re-reads the same page.

## The fork (the one fact this issue waits on)
Where do the per-model limits and the peak facts come from now?

- **(a) `GET https://opencode.ai/inference/go/v1/models`** — public, no credential (HTTP 200 to a bare client, 32 models, read 2026-11-18). Contrary to the dig finding, it **does** carry the limits: per model `go.monthly_usage: {"go": 100, "go-plus": 200, "go-teams": 105}` (`null` on the free models), and the peak facts as `cost.multipliers[]` (`when.utc_days.in: [mon..fri]`, `utc_hours` 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00, `factor: 2`), plus `cost.text` base rates. The Plan fees and the window shares stay on `go.mdx`. **But this is the rail's own models list, and the operator's ruling of 2026-11-12 on #2768 says "The rail's `/zen/go/v1/models` answer stays unread: no third read, no `served` flag, no reference price"** — written into GW-CATALOG-GO as "The leg does not read that list". That ruling was about *listing* (the rail serving an id is not an allowance); reading the same answer for *limits only* keeps its intent but not its letter. Amending it is the operator's.
- **(b) Console's Go page** `https://opencode.ai/console/go` — public HTML (200, 153 kB), client-rendered; a scrape of a JS app, more brittle than the page it replaces.
- **(c) Pin the docs read to the last vendor commit that has the tables** — the alerts clear, and the limits silently stop following the vendor: the staleness alert would no longer mean anything for this source.

Intake's lean: **(a)**, limits and peak facts only — the listing stays models.dev under the console's overlay, no `served` flag, no reference price, an id on that list the catalog does not list stays unlisted. It is the only option that is a machine-readable vendor source.

## If (a): the shape of the work (draft, for the re-rule)
- `docs` stays ONE source with two reads, as `config` already is: the page read (`go.mdx` — Plan fees, the share bullets) and the limits read (`/inference/go/v1/models`, no credential). The snapshot's and the view's shape do not change (`catalog.schema.json` `docs_snapshot` keeps its keys), so the alerts, the metrics and admission read what they read today.
- GW-CATALOG-GO: the §docs bullet, the strict paragraph, the #2768 ⚖ paragraph and the `⚑ gap: listed is not alive` row's last clause ("the rail's own `/models` answer stays unread") are edited; §What a fetch sends gains a fourth read row; the docs tables' knobs (`docs-unknown-model`, `docs-short-endpoint-row`, `docs-header-drift`, `docs-no-peak-hours`, `docs-shrunk`, `docs-promo`) describe page shapes that no longer exist and are re-cut against the two reads.
- GW-CATALOG-GO-PARSE: §What the page says, per model and §The page's constants keep their expected cells; their inputs name the new read.
- Unverified, verify during implementation: where the Nx `bonus` multiplier and the `(50% off)` promotion live now (`gemini-4-argon` carries `cost.multipliers: [{when: {date: {gte: "2026-12-01"}}, factor: 2}]` — the promotion spelled as a future price rise; no `bonus` key was seen on any row); whether a `go-teams` key under `monthly_usage` is passed over like the Plan row (#3011); whether the limits read needs the `User-Agent` the console read needs; the fixture is cut from a recorded answer (Goal #3300's `wire-quarry.py`), never hand-copied.
- The alert annotations in `argocd/resources/agent-gateway/prometheusrule.yaml` name `go.mdx` as the docs source and would name the second read (`classify_touches` → `machine-merge`, 2026-11-18).

## Out of scope
- The `config` source's own fault: `catalog: config fetch answered 403 (config read)` at 2026-11-17 21:45 and 2026-11-18 03:45 (last good 2026-11-17T15:45Z, 28 models); the console answers 401 to a bare probe. A different cause on a different read. `GoCatalogStale{source="config"}` follows at about 2026-11-18T15:45Z and is the next dig's. The 30-day Go key (FU-313) was due to expire 2026-11-16 — whether that is the 403 is not readable from the intake's seat; `gateway_credentials_rejected{rail="opencode"}` is 0.
- Modelling Go Teams (#3011's out-of-scope stands).
- #3293 (listed is not alive) — liveness stays the shadow cells' and the belts'.
